passages.text: A song. A Psalm of David.
passages.sermon: This is a song.\r\nThis is a psalm.\r\nDavid wrote this song and psalm.

passages.text: My heart is steadfast, O God; I will sing and make music with all my being.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this song.
\r\nDavid wrote this psalm.
\r\nDavid speaks to God.
\r\nDavid says his heart is steadfast.
\r\nDavid says, "O God, my heart is steadfast."
\r\nDavid will sing to God.
\r\nDavid will make music to God.
\r\nDavid will use all his being to praise God.
passages.original: שִׁ֖יר מִזְמ֣וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃ נָכ֣וֹן לִבִּ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים אָשִׁ֥ירָה וַ֝אֲזַמְּרָ֗ה אַף־ כְּבוֹדִֽי׃

passages.text: Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm as a song.
David speaks to musical instruments.
He says, “Awake, harp!”
He says, “Awake, lyre!”
David will play music early in the morning.
He will awaken the dawn with his music.

passages.text: I will praise You, O LORD, among the nations; I will sing Your praises among the peoples.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to the LORD.
David promises to praise the LORD.
David will praise the LORD among the nations.
David will sing to the LORD among all peoples.
passages.original: אוֹדְךָ֖ בָעַמִּ֥ים׀ יְהוָ֑ה וַ֝אֲזַמֶּרְךָ֗ בַּל־ אֻמִּֽים׃

passages.text: For Your loving devotion extends beyond the heavens, and Your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.
passages.sermon:
God shows loving devotion.
God’s loving devotion is very great.
God’s loving devotion is greater than the heavens.
God is faithful.
God’s faithfulness reaches to the clouds.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ גָד֣וֹל מֵֽעַל־ שָׁמַ֣יִם חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ וְֽעַד־ שְׁחָקִ֥ים אֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth.
passages.sermon:
God is the Most High.
God rules above the heavens.
God’s glory is great.
God’s glory fills all the earth.
passages.original: ר֣וּמָה עַל־ שָׁמַ֣יִם אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְעַ֖ל כָּל־ הָאָ֣רֶץ כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Respond and save us with Your right hand, that Your beloved may be delivered.
passages.sermon:
God loves His people.
\r\nGod calls His people His beloved.
\r\nGod has power to save.
\r\nGod uses His right hand to save.
\r\nGod, answer us.
\r\nGod, save us with Your right hand.
\r\nGod, deliver Your beloved people.
passages.original: לְ֭מַעַן יֵחָלְצ֣וּן יְדִידֶ֑יךָ הוֹשִׁ֖יעָה יְמִֽינְךָ֣ וַעֲנֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: God has spoken from His sanctuary: “I will triumph! I will parcel out Shechem and apportion the Valley of Succoth.
passages.sermon:
God spoke from His holy place.
God said, "I will rejoice.
I will divide Shechem.
I will measure out the Valley of Succoth."
passages.original: אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀ דִּבֶּ֥ר בְּקָדְשׁ֗וֹ אֶעְלֹ֥זָה אֲחַלְּקָ֥ה שְׁכֶ֑ם וְעֵ֖מֶק סֻכּ֣וֹת אֲמַדֵּֽד׃

passages.text: Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine; Ephraim is My helmet, Judah is My scepter.
passages.sermon:
God speaks from His sanctuary.
God claims ownership over certain tribes.
Gilead belongs to God.
Manasseh belongs to God.
Ephraim protects like a helmet for God.
Judah rules as God's scepter.
passages.original: לִ֤י גִלְעָ֨ד׀ לִ֤י מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה וְ֭אֶפְרַיִם מָע֣וֹז רֹאשִׁ֑י יְ֝הוּדָ֗ה מְחֹקְקִֽי׃

passages.text: Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I toss My sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks with authority and power.
God says, “Moab is My washbasin.
I use Moab for My purposes.
I throw My sandal on Edom.
I claim authority over Edom.
I shout in triumph over Philistia.
I show My victory over Philistia.”
passages.original: מוֹאָ֤ב׀ סִ֬יר רַחְצִ֗י עַל־ אֱ֭דוֹם אַשְׁלִ֣יךְ נַעֲלִ֑י עֲלֵֽי־ פְ֝לֶ֗שֶׁת אֶתְרוֹעָֽע׃

passages.text: Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
passages.sermon:
The speaker asks a question.
The speaker wants to reach a strong city.
The speaker says, “Who will bring me to the fortified city?”
The speaker also wants to go to Edom.
The speaker says, “Who will lead me to Edom?”
passages.original: מִ֣י יֹ֭בִלֵנִי עִ֣יר מִבְצָ֑ר מִ֖י נָחַ֣נִי עַד־ אֱדֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Have You not rejected us, O God? Will You no longer march out, O God, with our armies?
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David feels rejected by God.
David asks God a question.
David says, “God, have You not rejected us?”
David asks, “God, will You no longer go out with our armies?”
passages.original: הֲלֹֽא־ אֱלֹהִ֥ים זְנַחְתָּ֑נוּ וְֽלֹא־ תֵצֵ֥א אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים בְּצִבְאֹתֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Give us aid against the enemy, for the help of man is worthless.
passages.sermon: God, give us help against our enemy.\r\nThe help of people is useless.\r\nOnly God can save us.
passages.original: הָֽבָה־ לָּ֣נוּ עֶזְרָ֣ת מִצָּ֑ר וְ֝שָׁ֗וְא תְּשׁוּעַ֥ת אָדָֽם׃

passages.text: With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies.
passages.sermon:
God is with us.
We will act bravely because of God.
God will defeat our enemies.
God will crush those who oppose us.
passages.original: בֵּֽאלֹהִ֥ים נַעֲשֶׂה־ חָ֑יִל וְ֝ה֗וּא יָב֥וּס צָרֵֽינוּ׃
